title: Perseus: The Impossible Errand
subtitle: A king's trap, a promise of a Gorgon's head, and divine patrons

learningObjectives.text: What do the gods give him for the quest?

main.author: Pseudo-Apollodorus
main.note: Verbatim passage from the named work/translation; the locator selects this exact local source segment.
main.locator: Library 2.4.2, Polydectes and the wedding-gift trick
main.excerpt: Polydectes, brother of Dictys, was then king of Seriphus and fell in love with Danae, but could not get access to her, because Perseus was grown to man's estate. So he called together his friends, including Perseus, under the pretext of collecting contributions towards a wedding gift

narrativeBlocks.title: A wedding-gift scam
narrativeBlocks.body: Polydectes wants Danae and wants her son gone. He calls his friends together 'to collect contributions toward a wedding gift' — a polite ritual where everyone must offer a horse. Perseus has no horse to give.

narrativeBlocks.title: The fatal boast
narrativeBlocks.body: Cornered by pride, young Perseus offers instead any gift the king names — and Polydectes names the one thing that should kill him: the head of the Gorgon Medusa, whose gaze turns men to stone.

narrativeBlocks.title: Gods pick sides
narrativeBlocks.body: The quest is suicidal — but Perseus is Zeus's son, and Olympus supplies kit: Athena lends a mirrored shield, Hermes a curved blade, the nymphs give winged sandals, a magic knapsack, the cap of invisibility, and a bag for the head.

narrativeBlocks.title: The old women who share an eye
narrativeBlocks.body: To find the Gorgons he must first find the Graeae — three grey sisters born old, who share one eye and one tooth between them. Perseus snatches the eye mid-pass and ransoms it for directions.

narrativeBlocks.title: The equipped-hero pattern
narrativeBlocks.body: Perseus is the most kitted-out hero in the cycle — every impossible task is matched by a divine tool. Compare Theseus (bare hands, earned each step): two models of how a hero gets the job done.

quiz.prompt: How does Polydectes trap Perseus into the Gorgon quest?

choices.text: He collects 'wedding contributions' — Perseus can't offer a horse and rashly promises any other gift; the king names Medusa's head
He offers Danae's hand to whoever kills Medusa
He banishes Perseus until he returns with treasure
He loses a bet with Perseus at games

quiz.explanation: The errand is engineered to remove Perseus so the king can take Danae.

quiz.prompt: How does Perseus get directions to the Gorgons?

choices.text: He consults the oracle at Delphi
He steals the Graeae's single shared eye mid-pass and ransoms it for the route
Athena leads him directly to the island

quiz.explanation: The Graeae share one eye and one tooth — seizing the eye mid-handoff is the quest's first trick.
